facts.claim: "Deep In The Night" was released on 15 August 2023 as a standalone single, with the label credit 'Future Islands under exclusive license to 4AD Ltd'.
Its black-and-white music video was directed by Albert Birney.
The video shows the band performing the song in silhouette.
The band debuted the song in 2022 on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert.
Press described it as a slowed, romantic ballad with Samuel T. Herring's vocals over fluttery synths and electronic drums.
It was the band's first new music since the 2022 standalone single "King of Sweden".
Herring said the song was written with the idea that the couple's love would carry them to the end and he would find his partner. He said the couple split at the end of 2021.

Herring told NME the album's story centres on the break-up of his relationship with Swedish actress Julia Ragnarsson. He said the line 'When this ends I'll find you' in the song did not play out that way.
The song is track 3 (3:27) on the seventh album People Who Aren't There Anymore, released 26 January 2024 on 4AD.
The album was co-produced by Future Islands and Steve Wright. Wright and Chris Coady mixed it, and Coady also produced the band's 2014 breakthrough album Singles.

research.lineage: Future Islands are a Baltimore synth-pop/synth-rock band whose dramatic, ballad-leaning style, built around Samuel T. Herring's baritone and synths, is described by reviewers as part of indie synth-pop.

draft:
Partway through **Deep In The Night**, Samuel T. Herring stops singing "I belong to you" and sings "And I belonged to you." It's one past-tense verb at the end of a love song, and then the present tense comes rushing back: "I belong, I belong / To you." The slip lasts a single line, but the song turns on it.

The verses are set in the small hours. The singer lies awake beside a partner who is "still asleep" and somehow misses them anyway, from a few inches away. Herring reaches for a big image, "I'm like a prowling lion, that sinking pride," and the pun does real work. A pride of lions, and pride in the plain sense, going under together. The restlessness is half animal and half wounded ego. The tender part comes later: "it's the only time when I find peace," watching someone sleep. The chorus gives the whole self away with "And that's where I began," a person who only knows where they start by where someone else ends. Devotion and dread share the same bed here, and the song never picks one.

Herring has said he wrote it believing their love would carry them to the end and that he would find his partner. The couple split at the end of 2021, and he told NME that hope didn't play out. The song later became track three on *People Who Aren't There Anymore*, a 2024 record he has described as centred on the end of his relationship with the Swedish actress Julia Ragnarsson. Heard now, that one slip into "belonged" carries more weight than he could have meant.

The music doesn't brood. A synth bass walks under a drum machine's kick, snare, and hi-hat. A pad holds sustained chords, and a clean electric guitar picks arpeggios over the top. The groove is steady and driving, the tempo moderate, the production polished and smooth. Press called it a slowed, romantic ballad, and it is one, but it keeps a pulse you could walk to. Herring's voice sits mid-range with a slight rasp, carrying long melodic lines under a touch of reverb. It's a long way from his barking, chest-beating mode, and it's the Baltimore band's synth-pop at its most restrained. The arrangement holds its shape instead of swelling. Some will want it to break open. The restraint is the point.

Albert Birney's black-and-white video shows the band only in silhouette, which suits a song about someone you can see in the dark but not quite reach.

It sticks because it's a vow sung by someone who seems to sense, even while making it, that the person beside them is already slipping away, and you end up holding both feelings at once.

factCheck.note: Both quotes match the lyrics. 'Partway through' was changed to 'Late in the lyric', since the final stanza's position is shown by the lyric structure.
